finding: Grammar-only resolution rose from 2/31 to 21/31 and hybrid branches fell from 69 to 38. Fresh compilation lost to the fixed hybrid in the reported timing groups; shared-base reuse repaid after sampled batches of 4 or 8 queries.
limitations: The richer admission grammar was predeclared; it was not autonomously discovered.
Branch counts are not CPU time. Timing excludes research/design and independent exhaustive audits; small Python microbenchmarks are not general rankings.
Renaming and clause-order controls do not constitute independently sampled problems.

Preserved archive: MATH-GRAMMAR-DUAL-RUN-001-EVIDENCE-2026-10-15.zip. The attached files are inspection selections; they do not replace its complete runtime directory. No public archive URL or permission is implied. Full figures, historical versions and omitted dependencies remain in that archive.
method: The original miniature compares fixed unit propagation with predeclared certified parity relations, then tests 64 additive queries on each of two unchanged bases. The source, saved result ledgers, controls and CPU-accounting records are retained.
open_questions: Follow-on research remains separate from this completed record; exact publication review does not require a rerun.
